Description: A black limestone obelisk carved with tribute scenes from the reign of Assyrian king Shalmaneser III. One register shows a king of Israel kneeling before Shalmaneser, captioned as Jehu, 'son of Omri,' bringing tribute in about 841 BC.
BiblicalSignificance: It is the only known contemporary depiction of an Israelite king, and it confirms Jehu and the Omride dynasty from Assyrian records. Even in a scene of political submission, the stone preserves the names Scripture preserves, grounding Israel's kings in verifiable history.
Interpretations: Scholars agree the obelisk shows Jehu of Israel paying tribute to Shalmaneser III; the inscription calls him ‘son of Omri,’ using the dynasty’s name rather than his actual father.
